questions.question: According to the Census of India 2011, which metropolitan city has the highest population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **According to the 2011 Census of India,** **Mumbai** stands as the most populous metropolitan city in India, with a population of **18,394,392**.
 
• It is followed by **Delhi, Kolkata, and Chennai** in terms of population.
 
• Mumbai also holds the distinction of being the financial capital of India and serves as the capital of Maharashtra state.
 
• The city exhibits a remarkable population density, with approximately 21,000 individuals per square kilometer.
 
• The 2011 census of India was conducted in two phases: house listing and population enumeration, spanning from February 9 to February 28, 2011.
 
• The census revealed that the population of India at that time was 1,210,854,977.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The 2011 census of India, **also known as the 15th Indian census, was carried out in two phases: house listing and population enumeration.
 
• The House listing phase commenced on April 1, 2010, focusing on gathering information about all buildings. During this phase, data for the National Population Register (NPR) was also collected, aiming to provide a 12-digit unique identification number to all registered Indian residents by the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI).
 
• The second phase, population enumeration, took place between February 9 and February 28, 2011. Census-taking has been a tradition in India since 1872, and the 2011 census marked a significant milestone as it was the first time biometric information was collected.
 
• According to the provisional reports released on March 31, 2011, the Indian population had surged to 1.21 billion, reflecting a decadal growth of 17.70%. Moreover, the adult literacy rate had increased to 74.04%, showing a growth of 9.21% over the previous decade.

questions.question: What do the words ‘aus’, ‘aman’ and ‘boro’ signify in the context of agricultural calendar in India?

options.text: Types of seasons of sowing rice in West Bengal
Types of traditional wells in Gujarat
Types of alluvial soils in the Gangetic plains
Types of harvest festivals in Assam

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Types of seasons of sowing rice in West Bengal.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the context of the agricultural calendar in India, ‘aus’, ‘aman’, and ‘boro’ refer to three **distinct varieties of rice crops** that are grown in different seasons, particularly in the** eastern regions like West Bengal, Bihar, and Bangladesh.**
 
• **Aus**:
 
 
• **Season**: Sown in March-April and harvested in July-August.
 
• **Characteristics**: Aus rice is typically a **rain-fed crop** and is grown during the early monsoon period. It matures quickly and is often grown on upland areas.
 
 
 
• **Aman**:
 
 
• **Season**: Sown in June-July and harvested in November-December.
 
• **Characteristics**: Aman rice is grown in the main monsoon season and is **heavily dependent on the rains.** It is the most important rice crop in regions like West Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Boro**:
 
 
• **Season**: Sown in December-January and harvested in April-May.
 
• **Characteristics**: Boro rice is cultivated during the dry winter season with irrigation. It requires** controlled water supply **and is grown in low-lying areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Types of Traditional Wells in Gujarat

 
 
• **Vav/Stepwells:** These are intricately designed wells with steps leading down to the water. Famous for their architectural beauty, such as the Rani ki Vav in Patan.
 
• **Kua**: Traditional open wells used for drawing water manually, common in rural areas, and typically built near farms for irrigation.
 
 
 
• Types of Alluvial Soils in the Gangetic Plains
 
 
• **Khadar**: The newer, fertile alluvial soil deposited by rivers, found near riverbanks and floodplains. It is renewed annually during floods and is highly suitable for agriculture.
 
• **Bhangar**: The older alluvial soil found at higher elevations, slightly less fertile than Khadar due to the presence of calcium carbonate nodules (kankar).
 
 
 
• Types of Harvest Festivals in Assam
 
 
• **Bihu (Rongali Bihu)**: The most popular harvest festival, celebrated in April to mark the Assamese New Year and the start of the sowing season.
 
• **Kati Bihu**: Celebrated in October, during the mid-harvest season, focusing on protecting crops and seeking blessings for a good yield.

• The northeastern part of the country is marked by the presence of** big rivers, dissected relief, dense forests, frequent floods, landslides, international frontiers**, etc.

• **Railways:**

 
 
• **The first railway proposals for India were made in Madras in 1832.**
 
• As a result, the country got its first train in the form of the Red Hill Railway which was built with the sole purpose of transporting granite for road-building in 1837.
 
• In 1845, the Godavari Dam Construction Railway was built by Cotton at Dowleswaram in Rajahmundry, to supply stone for the construction of a dam over the Godavari River. 
 
• **India’s first passenger train, operated by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway and hauled by three steam locomotives – Sahib, Sindh, and Sultan – ran for 34 kilometers with 400 people in 14 carriages on 1,676 mm broad gauge track between Bori Bunder (Mumbai) and Thane on 16 April 1853.**

questions.question:
“It is a crop which is used both as food and fodder. It is a kharif crop which requires temperature between 21°C to 27°C and grows well in old alluvial soil.”

The above given statement talks about which of the following crops?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Maize**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Maize is a crop that is used both as food and fodder.

 
 
• It is a Kharif crop that requires a temperature between **21°C to 27°C** and grows well in **old alluvial soil**.
 
• In some states like **Bihar maize** is grown in the **rabi season** also.
 
• The use of modern inputs such as **HYV seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation** has contributed to the increasing production of maize.
 
• Major maize-producing states are **Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kharif Crops: Paddy, Jowar, Bajra, Maize, Ragi, Arhar(Tur), Moong, Urad, Cotton, Groundnut, Sunflower Seed, Soybean Black, Sesamum, Nigerseed.
 
• Rabi crops: Wheat, Barley, Gram, Masur (Lentil), Rapeseed/Mustard, Safflower, Toria.
 
• Other Crops: Copra, De-Husked Coconut, Jute, Sugarcane.

questions.question: According to the 2011 Census, any person aged _______ and above and has the ability to read and write is considered literate.
questions.solution:

__
 
• It was delayed to 2022 and then further delayed to 2023 due to the COVID-19 pandemic in India.
 
• Following the postponement of deadline of freezing administrative boundaries to 30 June 2023, and owing to the general elections in 2024, the census can now only take place in late 2024.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• The total number of literate persons in a given age group is expressed as a percentage of the total population in that age group.
 
• The **adult literacy rate** measures literacy among persons **aged 15 years and abov**e, and the** youth literacy rate** measures literacy among persons **aged 15 to 24 years.**
 
• As per the 2011 census, the literacy rate in India has been reported as 74.04% with a 14% increase from that in 2001.
 
• whereas the hike is maximum for rural women at 26% in the last decade.
 
• The female literacy levels according to the Literacy Rate 2011 census is 65.46% whereas the male literacy rate is over 80%.
 
• The literacy rate in the country is 74.04 per cent, 82.14 for males and 65.46 for females.
 
• The highest literacy rate according to the **2011 census is Kerala (93.9%) and Mizoram (91.6%).

questions.question: which of the following is the longest train route in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dibrugarh-Kanyakumari**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Dibrugarh-Kanyakumari** Vivek Express currently holds the title for the longest train route in India.
 
• It covers a distance of approximately **4,273 kilometers** from Dibrugarh in Assam to Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu.
 
• This train route traverses through multiple states including West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• The journey takes around **82 hours and 30 minutes**, making it one of the most extensive travel routes by train in the country.
 
• The Vivek Express was flagged off in **November 2011** and has since been an important link connecting the northeastern and southern parts of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India has a vast railway network, which is the fourth-largest in the world by size.
 
• The Indian Railways operates over **13,000 passenger trains** daily, connecting more than **7,000 stations** across the country.
 
• The **Indian Railways** is known for its efficiency in connecting remote and rural areas to major cities, playing a crucial role in the country's economy and mobility.
 
• The **Railway Budget** was merged with the Union Budget in 2017, marking a significant shift in the financial planning of the railway operations.
 
• Several initiatives like the introduction of high-speed trains, modernization of stations, and improvement in passenger amenities are continuously being undertaken to enhance the railway infrastructure in India.
